sourceContext: User explicitly prioritized finishing ORCHESTOR itself before any further Costa Clean application work. Tracker: GitHub Issue #23. This is a self-hosting ORCHESTOR-core completion command; Costa Clean application/product source is not an implementation target.
objective: Finish ORCHESTOR as a reusable, installable, multi-project local agent/controller. It must attach safely to arbitrary repositories, reuse one persistent Codex thread per project/workstream, execute commands autonomously through bounded review/repair loops, support multiple projects concurrently without cross-contamination, recover durably after restart, and notify the human only at genuine approval/safety gates or final completion.
why: The proven Costa Clean review/repair loop works, but ORCHESTOR is not yet certified as a generic hands-off multi-project tool. The user wants ORCHESTOR completed first, with no further Costa Clean product implementation during this command.
scope: Primary implementation target is the existing local ORCHESTOR source at C:\Users\USUARIO\orchestor. Do not treat Costa Clean application source as the implementation target.

First inspect and factually inventory the current ORCHESTOR architecture, registry, watcher, control-plane parser, Codex app-server adapter, persistent-thread bindings, isolated-worktree manager, result publisher, review/repair loop, restart recovery, notification path, tests and existing project bindings.

If self-targeting ORCHESTOR core is not yet representable by the runtime, implement the minimum safe self-hosting route locally in ORCHESTOR itself. Do not work around this by editing Costa Clean application source.

Create or complete a generic project registry able to register arbitrary repository roots, GitHub repositories/control locations, project/workstream IDs, canonical branches/baselines and exactly one persistent active Codex thread binding per project/workstream.

Provide a simple user-facing local workflow for add/register, list, status, doctor, start, stop/pause, resume and remove/disable project bindings. Prefer the existing CLI/config style; do not introduce a second orchestrator.
Preserve current Costa Clean project/workstream bindings and migrate them only if required by the generic registry. Migration must be backward-compatible and evidence-backed.

Implement independent per-project/workstream durable state: accepted Brain/context binding, StrategicCommand cursor, run ownership, isolated worktrees, review-loop state, results, interventions, locks and recovery metadata.

Support at least two registered projects/workstreams progressing concurrently. Concurrency must never mean concurrent use of the same persistent Codex thread; each project/workstream has its own thread lock and sequential turn discipline.
Enforce no cross-project contamination by repository identity, worktree root, branch, command hash, Brain/context, thread ID, run ID, result path and locks.

Complete the autonomous bounded loop: detect StrategicCommand, validate identity/authority, resume the correct persistent Codex thread, implement, run targeted/full verification, request/retrieve current-head review, classify actionable findings, repair safe in-scope findings, recertify and repeat.
Handle delayed GitHub/Codex review arrival robustly with bounded polling/backoff so the loop does not falsely stop merely because a review arrived after a short wait.
Keep bounded safety: maximum five repair/review cycles per phase, repeated-prompt/finding/workspace-fingerprint guards, and fail-closed escalation on no progress or ambiguous side effects.

Complete durable restart/recovery: after process restart, every project/workstream must resume only its own unfinished command/run without duplicate dispatch, duplicate thread creation, duplicate publication or cross-project state reuse.

Complete human-gate handling. Merge, production, Supabase remote, secrets, DNS, billing, payments, real external communications, destructive operations and material authority expansion remain explicit human gates.

Provide one durable intervention per genuine gate and a clear notification path. Reuse existing Windows/local notification facilities if present; do not require privileged Windows-service installation. A normal non-admin launcher/startup flow is acceptable if already supported.

Do not add any dependency on OPENAI_API_KEY, Responses API, Chat Completions API, Agents API or separately billed direct OpenAI API calls. Codex app-server/session authentication remains the model-execution path.

Create installation/onboarding documentation for attaching a new repository/project with the fewest practical steps, including how ChatGPT Project/StrategicCommand, GitHub control bridge and persistent Codex thread binding fit together.
Add a concise operator guide: register a repo, bind/reuse the existing Codex thread, start watcher, issue a StrategicCommand, inspect status, approve a human gate, and recover after restart.

Add automated tests for registry isolation, thread policy, command routing, locks, concurrency, review polling, repair-loop bounds, restart recovery, duplicate suppression, intervention idempotency and forbidden cross-project access.

Build an end-to-end certification using at least two isolated non-production fixture projects/workstreams. Demonstrate simultaneous queued/progressing work with independent threads/state/worktrees and zero cross-contamination.
In the certification, demonstrate one review finding flowing automatically through detection -> repair -> verification -> new review/result without manual prompt copy/paste.
In the certification, simulate/reproduce restart during an active run and prove exact safe resume with no duplicate side effects.
In the certification, exercise one genuine human-gate simulation and prove exactly one durable intervention/notification while the unrelated project continues safely.
Run complete ORCHESTOR tests, lint/typecheck/build if configured, security/secret checks, adversarial review and final end-to-end certification.
Use bounded autonomous Planner -> Executor -> Verify -> Review -> Repair iterations until all completion criteria pass or a genuine human approval/safety blocker is reached.
Update GitHub Issue #23 with milestone evidence and a final completion report. Publish factual ORCHESTOR control/result evidence without changing Costa Clean application/product source.
When PROJECT_COMPLETE=YES, leave the system in normal usable mode with exact next-use instructions and no routine copy/paste requirement between ChatGPT and Codex.
outOfScope: Costa Clean product/application feature implementation, including N5.3/N5.4/N5.5 or any other app roadmap work.
Any change to Costa Clean business logic, UI, migrations, Supabase schema/data or production behavior.
Application PRs/merges/releases unrelated to ORCHESTOR core.
Vercel production deployment or intentional application deployment.
Real provider/OCR integration, API keys, secrets, billing or financial actions.
Creating a second orchestrator implementation or duplicate agent framework.
Creating a second active Codex thread for a project/workstream that already has a valid persistent thread.
Privileged Windows service installation, system-wide policy changes or destructive machine configuration.
acceptanceCriteria: PROJECT_COMPLETE=YES is supported by an end-to-end certification, not only unit tests.
A generic project registry can attach at least two arbitrary isolated fixture repositories/workstreams without Costa Clean-specific hard-coding.
Exactly one persistent active Codex thread is maintained per registered project/workstream and is reused sequentially.
Two projects/workstreams can make progress concurrently while all command/run/worktree/thread/result/intervention state remains isolated.
No cross-project contamination is observed under normal, adversarial, restart and concurrent execution tests.
StrategicCommands are detected automatically and routed to the correct project/workstream/thread without routine human copy/paste.
Current-head reviews are polled/retrieved robustly and delayed review arrival does not falsely terminate the loop.
Safe in-scope review findings are automatically repaired through bounded review/repair iterations.
Restart recovery resumes exactly the correct unfinished work without duplicate dispatch/publication/thread creation.
Human-gated actions produce one durable intervention/notification and do not block unrelated safe projects.
No direct OpenAI API billing path or OPENAI_API_KEY dependency is introduced.
Registration/onboarding, status/doctor, start/stop/resume and recovery workflows are documented and tested.
Existing Costa Clean ORCHESTOR bindings remain valid or are migrated with explicit tests and no application source mutation.
Complete ORCHESTOR tests and configured lint/typecheck/build/security checks pass.
Independent/adversarial final review reports no unresolved correctness/security findings.
Final Issue #23 report includes installation/use steps, certification evidence, remaining human gates (if any), and PROJECT_COMPLETE=YES.
During this command, Costa Clean application/product source mutation count is zero and production/Supabase remote mutation count is zero.
requiredApprovals: Any production deployment or production mutation.
Any new secret, credential, DNS, billing, payment or real external communication.
Any material expansion beyond ORCHESTOR-core completion and non-production fixture certification.
stopConditions: Costa Clean application/product source would need to be changed.
A production, Supabase remote, secret, billing, payment, DNS, destructive or real external side effect becomes necessary.
Self-targeting ORCHESTOR core cannot be established without ambiguous repository ownership or unsafe mutation.
The runtime cannot prove project/workstream/thread/worktree isolation.
A new Codex thread would be required where a valid bound thread already exists.
Any cross-project contamination is observed and cannot be repaired safely inside ORCHESTOR core scope.
A final unresolved correctness/security finding remains after allowed repair cycles.
A privileged Windows change is the only remaining way to meet completion.
verificationRequirements: Record the exact ORCHESTOR source root, repository identity if any, starting HEAD/state and all modified ORCHESTOR files.
Prove Costa Clean application/product source diff remains zero for this command.
Prove no Supabase remote or production mutation and no intentional Vercel production deployment occurs.
Run and pass multi-project concurrency tests with at least two independent fixture projects/workstreams.
Run and pass delayed-review polling and bounded auto-repair tests.
Run and pass restart/recovery and idempotency tests.
Run and pass human-gate/intervention idempotency tests while unrelated work continues.
Run full ORCHESTOR test suite and configured lint/typecheck/build/security checks.
Run an end-to-end two-project certification demonstrating command detection, correct thread routing, isolated worktrees, automatic repair loop, durable result publication and restart recovery.
Perform independent/adversarial final review and require no unresolved correctness/security findings.
Update Issue #23 with final evidence and usage instructions.

Final report must include PROJECT_COMPLETE, MULTI_PROJECT, MANUAL_COPY_PASTE_REQUIRED, DIRECT_OPENAI_API_USED, THREAD_POLICY, REVIEW_REPAIR_LOOP, RESTART_RECOVERY, HUMAN_GATES, NOTIFICATIONS, TESTS, FINAL_CERTIFICATION, APP_SOURCE_MUTATIONS, PRODUCTION_MUTATIONS and REMAINING_BLOCKERS.
